RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors authorizes the General Manager to execute the attached Agreement of Lease for Food
and Beverage Operations at the Tahoe City Golf Course/Winter Sports Park (Property) with Café Zenon
(Tenant).

BACKGROUND:

Café Zenon has operated food and beverage service at the Property since October 2016 as a cooperative
partner of the District, in accordance with the terms of consecutive agreements.
In April 2019, following expiration of the initial agreement, staff worked with Café Zenon to develop a
mutually beneficial agreement to provide the continuation of food and beverage services at the clubhouse
while the District completed its planning process for future clubhouse replacement/renovations. Due to
delays associated with the clubhouse project, the District and Café Zenon have extended the lease multiple
times. Since March 2024 has operated under a month-to-month continuation of existing lease terms.
The terms and conditions of the attached Agreement are substantially the same as the previous agreement,
with the exception of the following key provisions:

 TO:          Board of Directors                 DATE:   September 4, 2026

 FROM:        Sean Barclay                       SUBJ:   Employee Recognition – CSDA Staff Member of
              General Manager                            the Year Award

RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors recognize Director of Strategic Affairs Kim Boyd for receiving the 2026 Staff Member
of the Year Award from California Special Districts Association (CSDA).

BACKGROUND:

CSDA has named Director of Strategic Affairs Kim Boyd as the 2026 Staff Member of the Year. This
prestigious award honors one special district staff member who has demonstrated outstanding public service
and made a measurable contribution to their district and community, as well as advancing and positively
impacting the mission of special districts statewide.

Kim began her career with TCPUD in 2017 as a Senior Management Analyst and was promoted to Director of
Strategic Affairs in January 2024. Kim’s quiet leadership, deep commitment to the District’s Core Values and
unique display of initiative and tenacity have made significant contributions to the District, our community
and the entire statewide water agency community.

Kim’s leadership extends well beyond the accomplishments associated with her position. She has become a
trusted mentor and resource to leaders throughout the District, particularly those who are newer to their
roles and have looked to Kim for guidance, perspective, and institutional knowledge as they navigate the
responsibilities and challenges of leadership. Kim is generous with her time and expertise, readily offering
thoughtful and candid feedback, sharing lessons learned from her own experience, and stepping in to support
colleagues even when the issue falls outside her direct area of responsibility.

Notable among her many accomplishments are Kim’s work to secure more than $15.6 million

RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors authorize the General Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement (PSA)
with ClientFirst for a Virtual Chief Information Officer (vCIO).

BACKGROUND:

At the March 21, 2025, Board meeting, the Board authorized the General Manager to execute a professional
services agreement with ClientFirst for the development of an IT Strategic Plan. The IT Strategic Plan has been
a District Operational Priority, and is planned for completion in 2026. The goals of the IT Strategic Plan include
a roadmap for technology initiatives with clear objectives to guide the District's technology direction, including
budgeting, prioritization, and resource allocation. The Board will receive full presentation of the IT Strategic
Plan at the September 18, 2026, Board meeting. Recommendations from the IT Strategic Plan will include
staffing and support recommendations in addition to increasing the IT budget to meet industry standards.

As part of the staffing and support recommendations, a temporary vCIO is recommended to support, train, and
mentor the IT Administrator and the Director of Finance & Administration. The vCIO will also guide
management and IT staff on best practices for all areas of IT, provide assistance on current IT projects, and
provide vendor management support.

 TO:         Board of Directors                      DATE:      September 1, 2026
 Cc:         Parks & Recreation Committee
 FROM:       Kim Boyd                                SUBJ:      Discussion on the Community Meeting for
             Interim Director of Parks and                      the Tahoe City Community Center Planning
             Recreation                                         and Feasibility Study Project

RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors review and discuss the proposed format for a community meeting for the Tahoe City
Community Center Planning and Feasibility Study Project (Project) and provide feedback and direction on the meeting
structure, polling questions, Board participation, and public comment process.

BACKGROUND:

The Board continues to evaluate future active recreation opportunities at the Tahoe City Community Center (TCCC)
property through the Project. The planning and feasibility work has considered three potential recreation facility
concepts: an indoor recreation facility, an indoor aquatics facility, and a combined recreation and aquatics facility. The
concepts have been developed at a programmatic level and have been used to frame ongoing community engagement
regarding recreation priorities, facility preferences, and potential funding approaches.

On August 21, 2026 the Board directed staff to plan a community meeting to provide an interactive opportunity for
community members to ask questions and share comments on the proposed recreation concepts at the TCCC property.
The meeting is not intended to result in a final project decision or serve as a formal vote on any facility concept or
funding measure. Rather, the purpose is to gather additional qualitative and quantitative input to help inform future
Board direction on whether, and how, to advance the Project.

TAHOE CITY PUBLIC UTILITY DISTRICT
                                                               MEMORANDUM


    TO:       Board of Directors                       DATE:    September 9, 2026

    FROM:     Sean Barclay                             SUBJ:    Adopt the TCPUD Strategic Plan - 2027-2031
              General Manager


RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors adopt the TCPUD Strategic Plan - 2027-2031.

BACKGROUND:

The TCPUD Strategic Plan - 2027-2031 (Plan) establishes the District’s vision, priorities, and direction for the
next five years. It is the culmination of a comprehensive, months-long planning process that included small-
group engagement with front-line staff, a supervisory and professional staff workshop, and a senior
management workshop. Input was collected and refined through these staff-led efforts and informed the draft
2027-2031 Strategic Plan Priorities and Core Operating Principles, which were presented for the Board’s
review and discussion at the July 31, 2026 Special Meeting of the Board of Directors. The Board discussed
both documents in detail and provided feedback and direction, and directed staff to incorporate that feedback
and prepare updated versions for further review at the August Board meeting.

At the August 21, 2026 Board Meeting, the Board reviewed the draft Plan and directed staff to bring it
forward for final adoption at the September Board Meeting.

The Plan is organized around five Strategic Focus Areas: Governance, Management & Organizational Health;
Safe & Sustainable Water & Sewer Services; Outstanding Recreation & Leisure Opportunities; Resilient
Infrastructure & Facilities; and Long-Term Financial Sustainability. Within each, the Plan sets a focused set of
high-level Priorities, with specific Objectives that define the work needed to achieve them. It also includes the
District’s Core Operating Principles, which describe the standards and practices that guide how the District
conducts its business every day.

                                                             MEMORANDUM


 TO:          Board of Directors         DATE:         September 1, 2026
 FROM:        Sean Barclay               SUBJ:         2027 Training and Conference Opportunities for Board
              General Manager                          of Directors – Discussion for 2027 Budget

RECOMMENDATION:

The Board of Directors review and discuss 2027 training and conference opportunities and provide direction
on the allocation of funds in the 2027 District operating budget for the Board’s participation.

BACKGROUND:

The following is a list of regular training and conference opportunities available for ongoing Board member
development. These events are frequently attended by staff and Board members from a variety of local
agencies and special districts each year and offer valuable education in governance, leadership, legislative
affairs, and industry best practices.

Association of California Water Agencies (ACWA/JPIA) Spring and Fall Conferences – Statewide water
conferences covering water policy, regulatory updates, and risk management topics.

California Special Districts Association (CSDA) – Offers a variety of conferences and training
opportunities:
    • CSDA Annual Conference and Exhibitor Showcase – Focused on governance, best practices, and
        networking with other districts.
    • CSDA General Manager Leadership Summit – Leadership development and emerging issues for
        district leaders.
    • Special District Legislative Days – Legislative and advocacy with direct engagement opportunities at
        the State Capitol.
    • Special District Leadership Academy Conference – Comprehensive governance training designed for
        both new and experienced board members. Curriculum emphasizes the board–general manager
        partnership, effective leadership, and core governance responsibilities.
